thread:
ali: Noticed higher perceived latency for streaming clients after yesterday's runtime kernel tweak. p95 up ~40ms, p99 up ~120ms. Anyone else?

maria: Yep. Seeing it on long convs (>800 tokens). Feels like chunk flush interval interacting badly with microbatching + KV eviction.

kevin: Profiling glance: we see fallback to generic kernel at the tail when seq_len spikes, and batching queue delays around the same time.

perf-bot: perf summary: https://perf.redwood/abcd - text-generation-stream p95 180ms -> 220ms, p99 regressed ~120ms.

jess: Do we have runtime config for the failing fleet? flush_ms / chunk_tokens / microbatch?

ali: Default fleet config: chunk_tokens=8, flush_ms=100, microbatch=16. I ran a local sim with chunk=4, flush=50, microbatch=8 and observed lower perceived first-byte latency.

maria: Interesting. Throughput dropped ~8% in your sim, but KV cache hit ratio improved slightly (less partial KV writes).

kevin: Quick paste from profiler timeline:
```
[timeline] req 0: enqueue 0.0ms
emit_chunk: queued 50ms
kernel_select: optimized_matmul chosen 2.4ms
kernel_select: fallback_generic 48.2ms (when seq_len>1024)
kv_write: 5.1ms
total first-byte: 112.7ms
```

maria: That fallback is the culprit. When fallback happens the thread stalls and the microbatch queue piles up -> head-of-line blocking -> perceived latency spikes.

ali: @kevin can we avoid that fallback? Maybe prefer the optimized kernel even when seq_len borderline? Might OOM though.

kevin: There's a runtime flag `--prefer-optimized-kernels`. It forces the fast path but can raise memory by ~6-10% on some quantized models. We can gate it behind a canary. Also another idea: dynamic chunking — small chunks during high-variance early tokens, then increase once seq stabilizes.

jess: We should A/B test: (A) chunk=4, flush=40, microbatch=8 (B) chunk=8, flush=100, microbatch=16 (C) adaptive (start 4 -> ramp to 16). 10% traffic for 6h windows.

ops-bot: Canary schedule created: deploy rtd-20260316-ck1 -> eu-west, 10% traffic, 03:00-09:00 UTC.

maria: Add metrics to the dashboard: client_perceived_first_byte, backend_first_byte, kernel_fallback_rate, kv_write_ops_per_token, gpu_utilization. Want drilldowns by seq_len bucket.

ali: I pushed a repro script to infra: `./run_stream_load --model redwood-open-7b --clients 200 --chunk=4 --flush_ms=40 --microbatch=8` — can reproduce locally within ±10ms of the canary numbers.

kevin: One more observation: very small chunk sizes increase KV write amplification (more KV updates per token) and more PCIe traffic. That can hurt throughput and increase tail latency under load. So there's a tradeoff: smaller chunk -> better perceived latency at low load, worse GPU/PCIe efficiency at high load.

jess: Proposed plan:
1) Canary adaptive chunker (start 4 tokens, ramp to 16 after stable emit)
2) Gate `--prefer-optimized-kernels` behind canary to reduce fallback spikes
3) Update telemetry and add p95/p99 regression alerts for streaming-first-byte
4) Add perf guard that rejects kernel flag if OOM observed in canary
Assign: kevin (kernel change), maria (telemetry + canary config), ali (load tests + repro), jess (runbook + rollout).

ali: I'll run the A/B today and post numbers here after the 6h run. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jess: If the canary looks clean we should also bake adaptive chunking into the per-model profile so customers get better defaults.

maria: Agreed. Also add a note in the console docs about chunk/flush tradeoffs (link to runbook) so solutions engineering can advise customers.

kevin: I'll prepare kernel guard so it auto-rolls back if OOM or fallback rate > 0.5% in 5m window.

ali: Sounds good. Follow-up thread after canary.
